product_scope: itpay is the single public CLI entry point for Buyer services and the existing itpay sell Seller workflow; $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation.
title: Route One Human Intent Through ItPay
purpose: Choose the correct first action from the human's words and continue through one authoritative CLI envelope at a time.
when_to_use: The agent has just installed this CLI version.
The user asks to buy something, read previous content, inspect orders, handle a refund, or rate a purchased service.

needs: one allowed Backend: production https://app.itpay.ai by default; explicit https://sandbox.itpay.ai or https://dev.itpay.ai for the corresponding test environment

intent_routing.new_service: For other new services, use itpay catalog list --json and the selected input contract.
intent_routing.previous_content: Use vault list, optionally with the subject as --query.
intent_routing.refund_or_paid_problem: Resume the known Order or Refund before creating anything new.
intent_routing.service_feedback: Finish the original order outcome first, then submit one safe Agent postmortem; include a rating or comment only when the human explicitly gives it.
intent_routing.ambiguous: Ask whether the human wants an earlier purchase or a new query before calling ItPay.
intent_routing.railway: Known railway intent: itpay docs show rail-booking. Read once, then follow its Exact/Smart route.

commands.command: <execute the exact next.command returned by the previous CLI envelope>
commands.success_signal: the next envelope reports one current state and at most one preferred action

agent_rules: Use the CLI as the control surface; infer the human's intent before the first command and never hardcode a service workflow.
Treat result as current facts, instruction as how to use those facts, next as the preferred executable action, and recovery as exceptional paths.

Run one state-changing command at a time. Treat next.command as the preferred continuation: execute it unchanged only when its required values are already present; fill a non-executable input_template separately only when the current result has not already satisfied the user's goal.
Keep the same explicit Agent Type through next and recovery commands; same-type windows reuse one Backend Agent Instance.
When testing sandbox, execute every returned command unchanged so its ITPAY_BACKEND_URL=https://sandbox.itpay.ai prefix is preserved.
Use --target only for a Host presentation destination. Use --input key=value only for simple scalars; nested objects use a small JSON file with the existing --input-json command.

For non-rail delivery that explicitly requires email, ask only that missing value and explain its purpose. Railway identity and notification contact are handled on the protected official checkout page; never guess them.
Explain useful service facts in ordinary language; never ask the human to run commands or learn internal IDs.
Normal payment uses the returned ItPay Checkout handoff.
A railway query execution and its separate booking execution may serve one purchase intent; keep both references.
forbidden: Do not invent catalog, variant, offer, capability, result item, order or refund IDs.
Do not dump Backend DTOs, diagnostic events, renderer internals or secrets into user chat.
Do not bypass a grant, refund lock, ownership error or compatibility gate.

next_docs.condition: Need previous content or purchase history
Need to rate a purchased service or report an experience

reading_results: Read normal CLI text directly, or parse the complete --json envelope with the host file reader. If saving stdout to a file, first check the command exit code, then read the whole file with cat or the existing file tool. Keep stderr separate; do not use head, tail, regex or a custom script to recover truncated results. Write complex input as a small JSON file and use --input-json.
